Eleven shared sources are cited by decisions in more than 8 different sprints within S001–S100.

I found them with a script. For each decision, it took the facts the decision is based on and used each fact's sprint scope. It then followed each fact's `derived_from` chain through parent facts until it reached a `shared-` source. Finally it counted the distinct sprints per source.

I kept only sources with a count above 8. `shared-19` has 9 sprints and `shared-11` and `shared-15` have 10 each. `shared-13`, `shared-16` and `shared-28` have 8 each, so they fall just short.
